Building a stateless MCP server with vector retrieval

By A. Researcher · 2026-07-21 · 8 min read

Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers traditionally hold session state in memory. This post walks through a stateless design that uses an external vector database for retrieval so the server can be scaled horizontally without sticky sessions.

Why stateless?

Stateful servers complicate deployment: rolling upgrades evict sessions, autoscaling needs warm pools, and observability becomes per-instance. Stateless servers trade a small retrieval latency for vastly simpler operations.

Architecture

The server holds three responsibilities: parse the incoming request, embed the query, and call the vector store. No conversation history lives in process memory.

Retrieval trade-offs

  • Top-k recall is bounded by the vector store's ANN index.
  • Re-ranking can be done out-of-band with a cross-encoder.
  • Cold-start latency depends on the embedding model.

Results

In a 1k-request/second benchmark on 8 vCPUs, p99 retrieval latency stayed under 80ms while the previous stateful design hit 320ms under the same load.

Code and benchmarks are available on GitHub.
